title: Movement, openings and clearances
intro: A cabinet can fit while closed and still fail in use. Map the body, moving parts and user route as separate overlapping zones.
goals: Check drawer extension and user position

sections.title: Map door movement
sections.text: Draw the cabinet body, hinge axis and intended door sweep in plan. Include the room door and nearby furniture. A sweep overlapping a fixed object or user route needs review. A closed-door image cannot establish sufficient opening for access to the contents.
sections.caption: The sweep reveals clashes with doors and routes.

sections.title: Check drawer extension and user position
sections.text: Mark the drawer front closed and at the required extension, then add the user position for retrieving contents. Use the selected runner data. Different runners, handles and contents can change the space needed; the extension alone does not represent the whole activity.
sections.caption: Add the user zone to the drawer extension.

sections.title: Check simultaneous-use cases
sections.text: Check credible simultaneous-use cases, such as a room door open while a drawer is in use. State which functions must operate together and any deliberate sequence. Do not add generic clearances without reading the plan. Recheck other access routes after changing the position or mechanism.
sections.caption: Recheck the alternative under required opening scenarios.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: An entrance door hits an extended drawer. The closed cabinet fits, but entry and drawer use cannot occur together as required.
example.decision: Decision: compare repositioning with another opening arrangement and test the entry route for both.

quiz.question: When should clearance be checked?
options: With body, movement and user in required scenarios
quiz.explanation: Clearance depends on movement and use, not the closed body alone.

assignment.prompt: Draw an entrance with a door and drawer cabinet; identify one clash and two corrective options.
criteria: Both options use the same scenario

faq.question: Should I immediately shrink the drawer?
faq.answer: Identify the cause first. A different position or opening direction may preserve the function better than reducing storage.
